repairs.description: Restored the documented 34-day event timestamp window and the rule that billable metrics match only events sent after metric creation.
Added product types, entitlement behavior, flat versus tiered rates, USD denomination, and rate effective-period controls needed to make the pricing stage query-useful.
Added the Ruby client-variable mismatch and cross-language contract-start-date mismatch so readers do not infer unsupported SDK differences from illustrative snippets.

Reorganized the happy-path workflow into event, metric, customer, pricing, and contract stages with an explicit boundary separating the introductory walkthrough from exhaustive API and lifecycle reference.
Mapped the guide to four planned domain concepts—event ingestion, billable metrics, products and rate cards, and customers and contracts—rather than creating a generic SDK concept.

contradictions.description: The Ruby setup names the client metronome but later Ruby examples call client; the canonical source records this as a sample caveat.
The Go contract example starts on 2024-09-01 while Python, Node.js, and Ruby use 2024-08-01; the canonical source treats the timestamps as illustrative rather than language-specific behavior.

review.notes: Read all 944 raw lines and the complete Luna output, draft, and worker receipt. Luna accurately captured the six-stage flow, SDK languages, client setup, major SDK features, ingestion batch limit and idempotency, metric operations, aliases, and draft-invoice update behavior. Sol added material lifecycle and pricing details, preserved two code-example inconsistencies as caveats, completed the concept audit before creating the source, and found no unsupported claim in the promoted page.
